clue.text: Sign seen at hen party?

definitions.meaning: the straight sense: a portent, a token of something to come
the joke: a hen party is for the bride and her female friends, so the male guest count is zero

explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a female-only celebration before a wedding, so the joke reads the answer as nought (O) plus a word for males.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent or sign foretelling something about the future.

clue.text: Very large copper can put in convict for bussing

parts.note: OS is the clothing size abbreviation for outsize
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the can is placed inside the convict

parts.note: an old lag is a convict
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A huge policeman can put a criminal on the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bussing' suggests buses, but to buss is an old word for to kiss; a lag is British slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Osculating is the formal or jocular word for kissing, which is what bussing means.

clue.text: These little mammals are I hesitate to say the pits!

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
mines are pits dug for coal or ore

explanation.surface: A speaker, reluctant, dismisses some small animals as awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pits' reads as slang for terrible, but it means mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermines are stoats, small carnivorous mammals, especially in their white winter coat.

clue.text: British sailors possessing deficiency, still getting stick

indicators.note: British sailors hold the next words between them, as one possesses what one holds

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
a lack is a shortage
tho is a short form of though, meaning still or nevertheless

explanation.surface: British seamen, short of something, still end up with a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackthorn wood is the traditional material for a walking stick or Irish shillelagh.

clue.text: Maybe healthy competition at first: everyone getting a buzz in the neighbourhood!

parts.note: lo-cal, low in calories, is one way food may be healthy

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: taken for its opening letter only
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A cheerful local sports contest gives the whole neighbourhood a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzz' suggests excitement, but it is a phone call; LO-CAL means low in calories.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzz is slang for a phone call, and a local call is one to a nearby number.

clue.text: Parties not exactly required by politicians

parts.note: ca., short for circa, means approximately
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Political parties that politicians do not strictly need.
explanation.definitionFit: Camps are factions or groups holding a shared view, as in the opposing camps of a debate.

clue.text: Journey on, taking it easy, finding protection from the elements etc

parts.note: a trip is a journey
in cricket the on side is the leg side
lazing is relaxing idly

explanation.surface: A traveller presses on in a relaxed way and finds shelter from the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so 'on' gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple glazing is three panes of glass in windows, insulating against cold, noise and so on.

clue.text: So Nelson had the Victory, I had heard

indicators.note: heard means the words are spoken, and the spoken sound gives the entry

parts.note: to have the victory is to have won, and I had contracts to I'd; together they are said aloud

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson, whose flagship was HMS Victory, triumphed, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: Victory was Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar, which hides the plain sense of winning; Nelson lost the sight of one eye in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson was blind in one eye after Calvi in 1794, so he was one-eyed.

clue.text: Issues with hotel food

parts.note: issues of a magazine are numbers, abbreviated nos

explanation.surface: Complaints about the meals in a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food or a meal.

clue.text: Withdrawing coat, one dropped embarrassingly short material

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so the coat's word is read backwards

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off the phrase it follows

parts.note: to drop a brick is British idiom for making an embarrassing blunder, so the thing dropped is a brick

explanation.surface: Someone takes off a coat and something embarrassingly short is revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: To drop a brick is a British idiom for committing an embarrassing gaffe.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, dense linen or cotton fabric, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Men probing underlying cause of fallen cradle? Dodgy old seat

indicators.note: the men get into the middle of the branch, as a probe goes inside

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Rock-a-bye Baby, when the bough breaks the cradle will fall; a rotten branch would break
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Investigators look into why a baby's cradle fell, and find a shady old chair.
explanation.walkthrough: A rotten borough was a pre-1832 parliamentary seat with almost no voters, controlled by a patron.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotten borough was a corrupt constituency, a dubious historical seat in Parliament.

clue.text: Misses Damien's manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres here are moves or reshufflings, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: the name and its possessive s are the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man called Damien's tactics fail to hit their target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misses' looks like a verb, but it is the plural of Miss, unmarried young women.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidens are unmarried girls, traditionally addressed as Miss.

clue.text: Wishes friend to get hold of incredible hit song

indicators.note: the yearnings grab hold of the next word, enclosing it

parts.note: to long is to wish or yearn
a tall story is one that is incredible
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a friend to get hold of an amazing hit record.
explanation.definitionFit: Long Tall Sally was Little Richard's 1956 rock and roll hit, later covered by the Beatles.

clue.text: Colour of sky pointer to storm

indicators.note: storming means raging wildly, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A finger pointing at the sky warns of a coming storm by its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Oyster pink is a pale pinkish-grey shade, like the inside of an oyster shell.

clue.text: Discrimination, not all from the Right, gets attention

indicators.note: reading from the right means the letters run backwards
only part of the words is used, so the letters sit inside them

parts.note: the letters sit across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A political point: prejudice from the right wing gets noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discrimination' suggests prejudice, but here it means discernment in choosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is the discernment to judge quality, a sense of discrimination as refined judgement.

clue.text: Setter's cornered daughter in lane, it's claimed

indicators.note: the jelly-and-daughter piece is placed inside the lane

parts.note: an alley is a narrow lane

indicators.note: the setter traps the daughter, holding her inside

parts.note: gel sets, so it is a setter; the 's is just 'has'

explanation.surface: A crossword setter boasts of trapping a daughter in an alleyway, or so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' points at the puzzle's author, but here it is gel, something that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegedly means reportedly or supposedly, as a statement made without proof.

clue.text: One taking inappropriate interest in single nurse we're told

indicators.note: we are told it by speech, so the spoken sound gives the entry

parts.note: lone means single, and the nurse shark is a species of shark; the pair is said aloud

explanation.surface: A person paying unwelcome attention to an unattached nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' seems a hospital worker, but it is a species of shark.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan shark lends money at extortionate rates, so takes excessive interest on loans.

clue.text: Things to observe after resorting to an alibi

indicators.note: re-sorting means sorting again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the second to in the clue, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone under suspicion falls back on an alibi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resorting to' reads as 'falling back on', but it is re-sorting the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Notabilia is a Latin plural for notable things, matters worthy of being noted.

clue.text: Problem caused by stream with river further down

indicators.note: in a down answer the river letter is shifted lower, toward the end

parts.note: a trickle is a small stream of liquid

explanation.surface: A problem arises with a stream as a river lies further downstream.
explanation.walkthrough: TRICKLE's R moves from second place to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tickler is a puzzling or delicate problem, as in a brain-tickler.

clue.text: Nothing, presumably, from Matthew on Grant

wordplay.note: the Bible from Matthew on is the New Testament, so none of it is the Old Testament; what remains

explanation.surface: A query about what Saint Matthew contributed to a grant.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew is the first book of the New Testament, so everything before it is ALL OT (Old Testament).
explanation.definitionFit: To grant something is to allot or assign it to someone.

clue.text: French mathematician's friend upset doctor

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the name alone is the definition

indicators.note: upset means overturned, which in a down clue reads the word upwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to doctor a drink is to lace it with something

explanation.surface: A French mathematician's friend upsets a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun, but it is the verb to adulterate.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Simon Laplace was a French mathematician and astronomer famed for the Laplace transform.

clue.text: One declining to follow vehicle — preferred one to go on foot

indicators.note: the decliner comes after the earlier pieces

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a pet idea or project is a favoured one
something that slips is declining or sliding down

explanation.surface: Someone falling behind a car prefers to walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To go on foot' suggests walking, but the definition is a thing worn on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet slipper is a soft indoor shoe, something worn on the foot.

clue.text: Unknown number removed from opposite side by a clear-out

indicators.note: the unknown is taken away from the opposing side

parts.note: the enemy is the opposing side
in algebra y is an unknown quantity
taken as written

explanation.surface: A team clears an unknown number of opponents out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear-out' suggests tidying, but it is the medical purge.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema clears out the bowel, a medical purge.

clue.text: That is muscle one would work on defiantly?

definitions.note: a person who carries on working in defiance of a strike

parts.note: sc. is short for scilicet, Latin for that is to say
abs are abdominal muscles, ab for short

explanation.surface: A gym-goer asks whether a muscle is the one to train stubbornly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work on' suggests exercising the muscle; SC (scilicet) means namely.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a strikebreaker, a worker who keeps working against a strike.

clue.text: One used to make yoghurt treat for consuming last month

indicators.note: the treatment swallows the month, holding it inside

parts.note: to cure is to treat successfully
ult., short for ultimo, means of last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: A recipe: yoghurt is a treat to eat by the end of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT (ultimo) is an old commercial abbreviation for last month.
explanation.definitionFit: A culture of live bacteria is the starter used to ferment milk into yoghurt.

clue.text: Ready for Asian broadcast again: HF

definitions.note: ready is slang for cash, so this is a cash unit for an Asian country

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written: high frequency, part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A radio operator is set to transmit on high frequency to Asia once more.
explanation.walkthrough: HF is high frequency, which fits the broadcasting picture; ready (readies) is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The afghani is the currency of Afghanistan, Asian money.

clue.text: Laughter and harsh cries as leaders swap personal flaws

indicators.note: the leaders are the first letters, which change places between the two words

parts.note: mirth is laughter and merriment
barks are harsh cries

explanation.surface: Laughter and harsh shouts as team captains change over.
explanation.definitionFit: Birthmarks are blemishes on the skin present from birth, a person's own marks.

clue.text: Eat little mushroom that's turned darkish at the centre

indicators.note: the mushroom is turned round, so read backwards

parts.note: a cep is the porcini mushroom

indicators.note: only the central letter of the word is used

parts.note: the middle of this seven-letter word is its fourth letter

explanation.surface: Eating only a little of a mushroom that has gone dark inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To peck at food is to nibble at it without appetite.
